About this document

This document provides the teaching content for Mathematics Years 12–13 of the
New Zealand Curriculum. Equivalent for Te Marautanga o Aotearoa is being
published separately.

Progress and assessment information for Mathematics Years 12–13 is still in
development. Once that is completed, Mathematics Years 12–13 is proposed to be
made by the Minister of Education as a National Curriculum Statement under section
90(1)(a) of the Education and Training Act 2020.

It is proposed that, once made and published in the New Zealand Gazette, schools
who offer Mathematics Years 12–13 will be required to start using it in Year 12 from
1 January 2029, and in Year 13 from 1 January 2030.

This document will be replaced with the official version made under the Act and
published in the New Zealand Gazette once that has occurred.

Purpose statement                                                  Ānō me he whare pūngāwerewere.   Behold, it is like the web of a spider.




  In Mathematics Years 12–13, students are taught fundamental principles of
  mathematics including advanced concepts like calculus, trigonometry, and
  algebraic techniques. They are taught how to develop mathematical reasoning
  and problem-solving through the contextualised study of mathematical concepts.


Through the study of Mathematics, students are taught to apply mathematical
knowledge and further develop numeric, algebraic, trigonometric, and mathematical
statistics concepts and application expertise. They apply principles and procedures to
solve problems, investigate relationships, and communicate mathematical ideas using
appropriate representations.

Mathematics provides students with the knowledge and practices to understand and
use mathematical symbols, notation, terminology, and visualisations. This disciplinary
knowledge enables students to evaluate and analyse mathematical expressions and
functions, solve equations, and test statistical hypotheses using critical and reflective
reasoning grounded in mathematics.
As students progress through Mathematics Years 12–13, they are supported to
develop their understanding of mathematical concepts and relationships and apply
calculations, techniques, and reasoning to increasingly sophisticated problems.


  Mathematical and statistical concepts form a strong foundation for life, work, or
  future study. Mathematics Years 12–13 leads to pathways in mathematics,
  finance, earth science, chemistry, physics, engineering, and technology.
